sentences.en: And she made this deal with him.
She said, you go to work with your father every summer and you learn to be a good bricklayer.
sentences.zh: 她说，你每年夏天都跟你父亲去工作，学会做一个优秀的泥瓦匠。

sentences.en: You go to MIT if you can get in and you learn to be a good civil engineer.
sentences.zh: 如果你能考上麻省理工学院就去上，学会做一个优秀的土木工程师。

sentences.en: When you finish, you can do whichever one you want.
sentences.zh: 等你毕业了，你想干哪个就干哪个。

sentences.en: That's how Salvucci wound up a student at MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
sentences.zh: 这就是萨尔武奇最终成为麻省理工学院（马萨诸塞理工学院）学生的经历。

sentences.en: One day in the early 1960s, he's sitting in class and a professor starts talking about a new highway project proposed for the city.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代初的一天，他正坐在教室里，一位教授开始谈论一项为该市提议的新高速公路项目。

sentences.en: It sounded an awful lot like the highway that had taken his grandmother's house.
sentences.zh: 这听起来非常像那条夺走他祖母房子的公路。

sentences.en: It was another piece of insanity, something that I was sure made no sense.
sentences.zh: 这是又一桩疯狂的行径，是我确信毫无意义的事情。

sentences.en: The difference was that this time, armed with that degree in engineering, Salvucci could actually do something about it.
sentences.zh: 不同的是，这一次，手握工程学位的萨尔武奇终于可以为此做点什么了。

sentences.en: So let's get the lay of the land.
sentences.zh: 让我们先来了解一下这里的地形。

sentences.en: There will be several highways you need to keep track of in this part of the story, but they all have a common origin, a master plan for the region drawn out way back in 1948.
sentences.zh: 在这个故事中，你需要关注几条高速公路，但它们都有一个共同的起源，即早在1948年绘制的该地区总体规划。

sentences.en: So if you could imagine something that highway planners often call a spoken wheel system, so you're looking at radio roads coming out of a center circle.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你能想象一下高速公路规划者通常所说的车轮辐条系统，你就会看到从中心圆圈延伸出来的无线电道路。

sentences.en: For the 1960s, a few pieces of that hub-and-spoke system had been built, but there were still, crucially, a handful of roads needed to complete the whole scheme,
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪60年代，这个轮毂辐条系统的一些部分已经建成，但至关重要的是，仍然需要几条道路来完成整个方案，

sentences.en: including something called the inner belt.
sentences.zh: 其中包括被称为内环的道路。

sentences.en: So when we think about the inner belt road, it's the heart of that wheel.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们想到内环路时，它就是那个车轮的心脏。

sentences.en: This is the road that Salvucci's professor was lecturing about, that Salvucci thought was absolutely insane.
sentences.zh: 这就是萨尔武奇教授在课上讲授的道路，也是萨尔武奇认为绝对疯狂的道路。

sentences.en: And he wasn't the only one.
sentences.zh: 而且他不是唯一的一个。

sentences.en: We said, no, no, no, no, no, no.
Anstey Benfield lived one block from the proposed route of the highway.
sentences.zh: 安斯蒂·本菲尔德住在距离拟建的高速公路路线一个街区的地方。

sentences.en: Right square in the middle of the line of the inner belt.
sentences.zh: 正好位于内环路线的正中间。

sentences.en: The road was supposed to start in Boston, then loop around into the neighboring city of Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 这条路原本应该从波士顿开始，然后环绕到邻近的剑桥市。

sentences.en: That is where Anstey lived, and where the whole region's highway fight would begin.
sentences.zh: 那是安斯蒂居住的地方，也是整个地区高速公路之战拉开帷幕的地方。

sentences.en: This part of Cambridge was largely working class.
sentences.zh: 剑桥的这个地区主要属于工人阶级。

sentences.en: People used to call it the greasy village, because historically, it had been the site of a massive factory that made soap from rendered pork fat.
sentences.zh: 人们过去常把它叫做油腻村，因为历史上，这里曾是一家用炼制猪油制造肥皂的大型工厂的所在地。

sentences.en: Then just down the road, you had the candy factories.
sentences.zh: 然后顺着路往下走，你就会看到糖果厂。

sentences.en: Necco wafers, Charleston chews, junior mints, all made in Cambridge, and all giving off smells of their own.
sentences.zh: Necco威化饼、查尔斯顿耐嚼糖、迷你薄荷糖，全都是在剑桥制造的，而且都散发着各自的气味。

sentences.en: So in the 1960s, you had a lot of longtime residents who had come to work the industrial jobs.
sentences.zh: 所以在20世纪60年代，这里有很多长期居住在这里的居民，他们是来这里从事工业工作的。

sentences.en: Immigrants from Ireland, Poland, Barbados, Panama, and black Americans coming up from the south.
sentences.zh: 来自爱尔兰、波兰、巴巴多斯、巴拿马的移民，以及从南方上来的美国黑人。

sentences.en: But this being Cambridge, Massachusetts, you also had the grad students and professors.
sentences.zh: 但既然这里是马萨诸塞州剑桥市，你也会看到研究生和教授。

sentences.en: The other side was the Hall of Harvard.
I mean a lot of Harvard.
That meant engineers, sociologists, highly educated troublemakers of all stripes.
sentences.zh: 这意味着工程师、社会学家、形形色色的受过高等教育的麻烦制造者。

sentences.en: Mayor Hayes, what is your objection to the abundance of hippies in Cambridge?
sentences.zh: 海斯市长，你对剑桥充斥着嬉皮士有什么异议？

sentences.en: The basic objection I have is the amount of them.
sentences.zh: 我的基本异议是他们的数量。

sentences.en: Noam Chomsky was lecturing at MIT.
sentences.zh: 诺姆·乔姆斯基当时在麻省理工学院讲学。

sentences.en: Joan Baez was singing protest anthems in Harvard Square.
sentences.zh: 琼·贝茨在哈佛广场高唱抗议歌曲。

sentences.en: Women's liberation, the Vietnam War, it was pretty fertile ground for an activist movement.
sentences.zh: 妇女解放、越南战争，这可以说是激进主义运动的绝佳土壤。

sentences.en: And a highway was the kind of issue that could bring everyone together,
sentences.zh: 而高速公路正是那种能够把所有人凝聚在一起的问题，

sentences.en: from Catholic priests and housewives to radical lefties and college students.
sentences.zh: 从天主教神父、家庭主妇到激进左翼分子和大学生。

sentences.en: I had my graduate degree in urban studies and I had a lot of energy and I needed something to do.
sentences.zh: 我拥有城市研究的研究生学位，我有着满腔热情，我需要找点事情做。

sentences.en: Well, lo and behold, within a year of buying that house on Chestnut Street,
sentences.zh: 好吧，说时迟那时快，就在买下栗树街那栋房子的不到一年时间里，

sentences.en: they started planning to knock the thing down.
sentences.zh: 他们开始计划把它拆了。

sentences.en: At that point, I went into action.
In early 1966, Anstie collected over a thousand signatures from other residents along the Interbelt Route.
sentences.zh: 1966年初，安斯蒂收集了内环路沿线其他居民的一千多份签名。

sentences.en: I took the pile of signatures and nailed them to the wooden doors of City Hall.
sentences.zh: 我把那一叠签名钉在了市政厅的木门上。

sentences.en: There's a picture of this in the local paper, the Cambridge Chronicle,
sentences.zh: 当地报纸《剑桥纪事报》上有一张关于此事的照片，

sentences.en: with Anstie carrying her two-year-old daughter on her back.
sentences.zh: 照片中安斯蒂背着她两岁的女儿。

sentences.en: Within two weeks, they changed the wooden doors to glass.
sentences.zh: 不到两周，他们就把木门换成了玻璃门。
但这个观点已经表达清楚了。

sentences.en: The residents of Cambridge would not go quietly.
sentences.zh: 剑桥的居民不会默默地逆来顺受。

sentences.en: Around this same time, Fred Salvucci set aside his bricklaying dreams for good.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时间，弗雷德·萨尔武奇彻底抛弃了他的泥瓦匠梦想。

sentences.en: He took a job as a transportation planner with the city of Boston.
sentences.zh: 他在波士顿市找到了一份交通规划师的工作。

sentences.en: His boss, the mayor, actually supported the Interbelt.
sentences.zh: 他的老板，也就是市长，实际上是支持内环的。

sentences.en: But Salvucci found that many of his fellow city planners did not.
sentences.zh: 但萨尔武奇发现他的许多城市规划师同事并不支持。

sentences.en: There was no game plan from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 从一开始就没有什么游戏计划。

sentences.en: We just sort of stumbled into it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是有点糊里糊涂地撞进去了。

sentences.en: One of those rogue city planners started writing pieces about the highway for the Cambridge Chronicle.
sentences.zh: 其中一位特立独行的城市规划师开始为《剑桥纪事报》撰写关于这条高速公路的文章。

sentences.en: Well, why has Cambridge got its head in the sand?
sentences.zh: 好吧，为什么剑桥要把头埋在沙子里？
为什么我们不提出替代方案？

sentences.en: There are questions about whether the road ought to be built at all.
sentences.zh: 关于这条路是否应该修建，一直存在疑问。

sentences.en: But certainly, if you're going to build it, it doesn't have to be this bad.
sentences.zh: 但当然，如果你打算修建它，它也不必修得这么糟糕。

sentences.en: And one day, a local priest reached out to the group.
sentences.zh: 有一天，一位当地的神父联系了这个小群体。

sentences.en: And said, gee, you are saying things that we're thinking in the neighborhood, but you've got technical skills that we don't have.
sentences.zh: 并说，天哪，你们说的话正是我们邻里心里想的，但你们拥有我们所没有的技术技能。

sentences.en: Would you be willing to work with us?
sentences.zh: 你们愿意和我们合作吗？

sentences.en: That call would change the course of the movement.
sentences.zh: 这个电话将改变这场运动的进程。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, we're like unpaid consultants working for the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我们就像是为社区工作的无薪顾问。

sentences.en: And I want to stress just how radical this was.
sentences.zh: 我想强调这有多么激进。

sentences.en: For years, states around the country had been telling residents, trust us, we know what's beSt.
sentences.zh: 多年来，全国各地的州政府一直对居民说，相信我们，我们知道什么是最好的。

sentences.en: Now, here were those same experts saying, no, the state is wrong.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些同样的专家却在说，不，州政府是错的。

sentences.en: Now, eventually, Salvucci's group got a name, Urban Planning Aid.
sentences.zh: 最终，萨尔武奇的小组有了一个名字，叫“城市规划援助”。

sentences.en: Did it feel like you were almost crossing enemy lines or something?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得自己几乎是在越过敌方防线之类的？

sentences.en: I mean, you're working for the city, and then you're moonlighting, helping residents and communities organized to oppose the city and state.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你为城市工作，然后你还在兼职，帮助居民和社区组织起来反对城市和州。

sentences.en: Were those things in tension for you?
sentences.zh: 这些事情对你来说有什么矛盾吗？

sentences.en: I'm not by nature a sneaky person.
sentences.zh: 我天性不是一个偷偷摸摸的人。

sentences.en: So I sent the memo to my boss and said, look, at night, this is what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 所以我给我的老板发了一份备忘录，说道，听着，晚上我在做这些事。

sentences.en: I'm working with people who don't believe in these highways.
sentences.zh: 我正在和那些不相信这些高速公路的人合作。

sentences.en: If you have a problem, let me know and I'll find another job.
sentences.zh: 如果你有问题，告诉我，我会去找另一份工作。

sentences.en: He said, well, no, we don't want you to go, but we want you to stop doing what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，不，我们不想让你走，但我们希望你停止你正在做的事情。

sentences.en: And I said, well, you don't have an option.
I do what I believe in.
He said, oh, you're crazy, but fine.
At that time, Salvucci was not convinced the inner belt could be stopped.
sentences.zh: 当时，萨尔武奇并不确信内环路能被阻止。

sentences.en: You're the governor, big construction companies, labor unions, not to mention a decade of unstoppable growth in the interstate system, all pushing to make the road happen.
sentences.zh: 你是州长、大建筑公司、工会，更不用说长达十年的不可阻挡的州际公路系统增长，都在推动这条路的建成。

sentences.en: So Salvucci was more focused on finding a way to make it less destructive so fewer families would have to lose their homes like his grandmother had.
sentences.zh: 因此，萨尔武奇更专注于寻找一种方法来降低其破坏性，这样像他祖母那样不得不失去家园的家庭就会减少。

sentences.en: That might sound like a modest aim, but it turned into a battle.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能是一个微不足道的目标，但它演变成了一场战斗。

sentences.en: Mr. Chairman, members of the city council, ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 主席先生，市议会议员们，女士们先生们。

sentences.en: This audio is from a Cambridge City Council meeting in 1966 discussing the impact of various routes.
sentences.zh: 这段音频来自1966年的一次剑桥市议会会议，讨论各种路线的影响。

sentences.en: I'd like to give a general description of the routes that have been considered as two possible or feasible alternates to the Brookline Elm route using the criteria which has been set up.
sentences.zh: 我想对被视为布鲁克林-埃尔姆路线的两个可能或可行替代方案的路线进行总体描述，使用的标准是已经制定的标准。

sentences.en: The route that the state was proposing was terrible, in Salvucci's opinion.
sentences.zh: 在萨尔武奇看来，州政府提议的路线太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It went straight through the neighborhood, the old greasy village.
sentences.zh: 它直接穿过了社区，也就是那个古老的油腻村。

sentences.en: If the plan was built, a sleepy one-way street lined with houses would be turned into an eight-lane elevated highway.
sentences.zh: 如果这个计划建成，一条两旁林立着房屋的沉睡的单行道将被变成一条八车道的高架高速公路。

sentences.en: The width that's required just for the structure would be roughly 135 feet.
sentences.zh: 仅结构本身所需的宽度就大约为135英尺。

sentences.en: But there was a logical alternative, which Salvucci's group was able to actually map out and publish.
sentences.zh: 但有一个符合逻辑的替代方案，萨尔武奇的小组实际上已经将其绘制并公布了出来。

sentences.en: It was just south of the original route, running along the path of old railroad tracks.
sentences.zh: 它位于原路线的正南方，沿着旧铁路线的轨迹延伸。

sentences.en: This is referred to as Scheme E or M.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的E方案或M方案。

sentences.en: It would take a fraction of the number of homes, but in a little twist of irony for Salvucci, it would go through the campus of MIT.
sentences.zh: 它将占用的房屋数量只是其中的一小部分，但对萨尔武奇来说有点讽刺意味的是，它将穿过麻省理工学院的校园。

sentences.en: And the present needs of MIT need to be considered.
sentences.zh: 而麻省理工学院目前的需要必须予以考虑。

sentences.en: This, of course, set many MIT types against him and this alternate route.
sentences.zh: 这当然让许多麻省理工学院的人站在了他的对立面，反对这条替代路线。

sentences.en: Salvucci recalls one critical moment, really a very Cambridge moment,
sentences.zh: 萨尔武奇回忆起一个关键时刻，一个非常具有剑桥特色的时刻，

sentences.en: when faculty from MIT and Harvard basically wound up debating the route issue,
sentences.zh: 当时来自麻省理工学院和哈佛大学的教职员工基本上最终在辩论路线问题，

sentences.en: upstairs at the Worst House in Harvard Square.
sentences.zh: 地点在哈佛广场的最糟糕的房子楼上。

sentences.en: On the neighborhood side was a Harvard economist named Kenneth Galbraith.
sentences.zh: 站在社区这一边的是一位名叫肯尼斯·加尔布雷斯的哈佛经济学家。

sentences.en: Now, Galbraith had just flown in from Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 当时，加尔布雷斯刚刚从瑞士飞回来。

sentences.en: That meant that Salvucci and another organizer named Jim Morey
sentences.zh: 这意味着萨尔武奇和另一位名叫吉姆·莫里的组织者

sentences.en: had only a few minutes to brief him on the details of the issue.
sentences.zh: 只有几分钟的时间向他简要介绍该问题的细节。

sentences.en: So he's just come off of a plane, and he's bleary-eyed, and he's bounding up the steps two at a time.
sentences.zh: 所以他刚下飞机，睡眼惺忪，正一步迈两级台阶地冲上楼梯。

sentences.en: Galbraith, by the way, was six feet, eight inches tall.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，加尔布雷斯身高六英尺八英寸。

sentences.en: Jim Morey is about five foot six, and he's running to keep up with Galbraith, and I'm two steps behind him.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·莫里大约五英尺六英寸高，他一路小跑跟上加尔布雷斯，而我就在他身后两步。

sentences.en: And talk about the elevator talk.
Morey briefs Galbraith in the space that it takes this giant to go two steps at a time
sentences.zh: 莫里在这样一个大块头一步迈两个台阶的时间里向加尔布雷斯做了简报，

sentences.en: from the ground floor to the second floor of the Worst House.
sentences.zh: 从最糟糕的房子的底楼到二楼。

sentences.en: So Galbraith says, I think I got it.
sentences.zh: 所以加尔布雷思说，我想我明白了。

sentences.en: The meeting begins, and a professor from MIT speaks firSt.
sentences.zh: 会议开始了，一位麻省理工学院的教授首先发言。

sentences.en: He basically said, look, I've been living here for a while now,
sentences.zh: 他基本上是说，听着，我在这里住了一段时间了，

sentences.en: and we keep trying to elect more progressive school committees and more progressive city councils.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在努力选出更多进步派的学校委员会和城市议会。

sentences.en: And every year, those people, that is the blue-collar population, get the majority.
sentences.zh: 而每年，这些人，也就是蓝领阶层，都会赢得多数席位。

sentences.en: And we have lousy education and a lousy government.
sentences.zh: 我们却得到了糟糕的教育和糟糕的政府。

sentences.en: And maybe, just maybe, if this highway knocks out 2,500 dwelling units and associated voters,
sentences.zh: 也许，哪怕只有一点可能，如果这条高速公路毁掉2,500套住宅和相关的选民，

sentences.en: maybe we'll win the next election.
sentences.zh: 也许我们就能赢得下一次选举。

sentences.en: The guy sitting next to him then makes a similar argument,
sentences.zh: 坐在他旁边的那个人随后提出了类似的论点，

sentences.en: that the road should go through the neighborhood, not the campus.
sentences.zh: 认为公路应该穿过社区，而不是校园。

sentences.en: At which point, Galbraith picks up his arm, which seems to almost reach the other side of the room,
sentences.zh: 就在这时，加尔布雷思举起手臂，他的手臂似乎几乎能够到房间的另一头，

sentences.en: points a finger, and says, only a moral imbecile would articulate such a cynical argument.
sentences.zh: 他指着对方说道，只有道德上的白痴才会说出如此冷酷无情的言论。

sentences.en: We're living in a country that's being torn apart by race,
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个因种族而撕裂的国家，

sentences.en: in a city that's being torn apart by racial strife.
sentences.zh: 在一个因种族冲突而撕裂的城市里。

sentences.en: And somehow, through some magic that none of us in this room are smart enough to understand,
sentences.zh: 不知何故，通过某种我们这个房间里谁也没有聪明到能够理解的魔力，

sentences.en: there's an integrated neighborhood here in Cambridge where people are getting along reasonably well,
sentences.zh: 剑桥这里有一个融合的社区，人们相处得相当融洽，

sentences.en: and they're low-income people and minorities.
sentences.zh: 他们是低收入人群和少数族裔。

sentences.en: And how on earth could we ever think of destroying this precious resource?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么可能哪怕有一丝一毫的想法去摧毁这个宝贵的资源？

sentences.en: And he just carries the day.
sentences.zh: 而他轻而易举地赢得了全场的支持。

sentences.en: These debates over the route were strategically important.
sentences.zh: 这些关于路线的辩论在战略上非常重要。

sentences.en: They bought time, drew attention, and made sure that the whole city of Cambridge had a stake in the issue.
sentences.zh: 它们争取了时间，吸引了注意力，并确保了整个剑桥市都与这个议题利害相关。

sentences.en: As long as the road could go anywhere, everyone had a reason to oppose it.
sentences.zh: 只要公路可能修在任何地方，每个人都有理由反对它。

sentences.en: But ultimately, the fate of the inner belt could not be decided in Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，内环路的命运不可能在剑桥决定。

sentences.en: This fight was bound for higher places, the governor's office, the White House.
sentences.zh: 这场斗争注定要走向更高层的地方，州长办公室，白宫。

sentences.en: The trouble is, the occupants of those high offices could always change,
sentences.zh: 问题是，那些高级职务的占有者总是会换人的，

sentences.en: and that would force the activists to change too.
sentences.zh: 而这也会迫使活动人士随之改变。

sentences.en: This election coverage is coming to you from WGBH-TV and WGBH-FM, Boston.
sentences.zh: 本次选举报道由波士顿WGBH电视台和WGBH广播电台为您呈现。

sentences.en: 1966 was an election year for governor.
And the man running to keep that job was named John Volpe.
sentences.zh: 竞选连任该职位的人名叫约翰·沃尔佩。

sentences.en: And he was a highway guy.
sentences.zh: 而他是个搞公路出身的人。

sentences.en: Before becoming governor, Volpe had owned a major construction firm and then served as the very first leader of the Federal Highway Administration under Eisenhower.
sentences.zh: 在担任州长之前，沃尔佩曾拥有过一家大型建筑公司，随后在艾森豪威尔手下担任联邦公路局的第一任负责人。

sentences.en: In Cambridge today, there is a mural that shows angry residents standing in front of a bulldozer.
sentences.zh: 如今在剑桥，有一幅壁画描绘了愤怒的居民站在推土机前的场景。

sentences.en: It's a little hard to tell just by looking, but if you ask Anstie Benfield, the man in the bulldozer is no other than...
sentences.zh: 光看外表可能有点难辨认，但如果你问安斯蒂·本菲尔德，推土机里的那个人不是别人，正是……

sentences.en: We're going to Volpe headquarters directly at this point.
sentences.zh: 我们现在直接前往沃尔佩竞选总部。

sentences.en: But urban planning aide scrambled to publish new data about the highways just beforehand.
sentences.zh: 但城市规划助理们在此之前争分夺秒地发布了关于高速公路的新数据。

sentences.en: And Joy is really broken out here at Volpe Richardson headquarters.
sentences.zh: 欢庆的气氛确实在沃尔佩·理查森总部爆发了。
沃尔佩的地位稳如泰山。

sentences.en: During the next four years, we will try to work as hard, if not harder, than we have during the past two years.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的四年里，我们将努力工作，其努力程度即使不超越过去两年，也绝不会逊色。

sentences.en: And again, as I say, place Massachusetts number one in all fields of endeavor.
sentences.zh: 再次如我所说，让马萨诸塞州在各个领域都名列第一。

sentences.en: So with a highway supporter firmly entrenched in the governor's office, the anti-highway activists now took their fight further up the ladder, to Washington.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着一位公路支持者稳稳占据州长办公室，反公路活动人士现在将他们的斗争提升到了更高的层面——华盛顿。

sentences.en: And within a year, we had four or five busloads of kids to Washington.
sentences.zh: 不到一年时间里，我们就把四五车厢的孩子们送到了华盛顿。

sentences.en: And, oh yes, I can tell you, we had signs that said, Cambridge is a city, not a highway.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，我可以告诉你，我们举着牌子，上面写着“剑桥是一座城市，不是一条高速公路”。

sentences.en: And all the kids started chanting, Cambridge is a city, not a highway.
sentences.zh: 所有的孩子们开始齐声高呼，“剑桥是一座城市，不是一条高速公路”。

sentences.en: They will never build roads through our homes.
sentences.zh: 他们绝不能在我们的家园上修路。

sentences.en: And we would holler these songs out all the way to Washington from Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 从剑桥到华盛顿的一路，我们都在大声喊着这些歌谣。

sentences.en: Anstey Benfield showed me another newspaper clipping.
sentences.zh: 安斯蒂·本菲尔德向我展示了另一份剪报。

sentences.en: Three kids sitting on the grass outside the Capitol with the headline, Lollipop Lobby.
sentences.zh: 三个孩子坐在国会大厦外的草地上，标题是“棒棒糖游说团”。

sentences.en: That was on the Washington Post front page.
sentences.zh: 那登在《华盛顿邮报》的头版。

sentences.en: I mean, that was the kind of thing that drew attention to our objections.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正是这种事情吸引了人们对我们反对意见的关注。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's hard to say no to 150 singing children.
sentences.zh: 是的，很难对150个唱歌的孩子说不。

sentences.en: The Lyndon Johnson administration ordered a pair of new studies on the inner belt, questioning both where the belt should go and whether it should be built at all.
sentences.zh: 林登·约翰逊政府下令对内环路进行两项新的研究，对内环路应该建在哪里以及是否应该修建提出了质疑。

sentences.en: It was a huge win for Benfield, Savucci, and all the anti-highway folks.
sentences.zh: 这对本菲尔德、萨武奇以及所有反公路人士来说是一场巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: But just as those studies began, the whole game was turned on its head.
sentences.zh: 但就在这些研究开始之际，整个局势发生了翻天覆地的变化。

sentences.en: It's time for new leadership for the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 是时候为美利坚合众国引入新的领导层了。

sentences.en: In 1968, Richard Nixon was running for president.
sentences.zh: 1968年，理查德·尼克松正在竞选总统。

sentences.en: And in the words of one Boston Globe reporter, Governor John Volpe was running right after him.
sentences.zh: 用《波士顿环球报》一位记者的话来说，约翰·沃尔佩州长紧随其后追了上去。

sentences.en: Volpe was tired of Democrats in Washington holding up the inner belt.
sentences.zh: 沃尔佩厌倦了华盛顿的民主党人对内环路的阻挠。

sentences.en: So he set out to replace them with himself.
sentences.zh: 因此他着手用自己取代他们。

sentences.en: When Richard Nixon becomes president, he immediately taps Volpe to be the head of transportation in D.C.
sentences.zh: 当理查德·尼克松当选总统时，他立即任命沃尔佩担任华盛顿特区的交通负责人。

sentences.en: Secretary of Transportation for the whole country.
Volpe gave a speech after the election in which he spoke about the inner belt and told the crowd with confidence,
sentences.zh: 沃尔佩在选举后发表了一次演讲，其中谈到了内环路，并充满信心地对人群说，

sentences.en: there's a new administration taking office in Washington, and I think we'll start to see things happen.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿正在迎来一个新政府，我认为我们将开始看到事情发生变化。
再次感谢作家卡洛琳·克罗克特。

sentences.en: So Volpe gets whisked away, and quickly his second-in-command becomes governor.
sentences.zh: 于是沃尔佩被调走了，他的副手很快成为了州长。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, the activists' allies in Washington had been replaced by their foe in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，活动人士在华盛顿的盟友被他们在马萨诸塞州的死敌所取代。

sentences.en: And their foe in Massachusetts had been replaced by a question mark.
sentences.zh: 而他们在马萨诸塞州的死敌则被一个问号所取代。

sentences.en: The question mark's name was Francis Sargent.
sentences.zh: 这个问号的名字叫弗朗西斯·萨金特。

sentences.en: So when Francis Sargent would become governor in this surprise, almost sleight-of-hand move,
sentences.zh: 因此，当弗朗西斯·萨金特通过这种几乎带有戏法性质的意外举动成为州长时，

sentences.en: the thought on the ground was, hmm, we have maybe an opening here.
sentences.zh: 基层民众的想法是，嗯，我们这里也许有了一个突破口。

sentences.en: At the same time that the debate over the inner belt is playing out in Cambridge,
sentences.zh: 就在围绕内环路的辩论在剑桥展开的同时，

sentences.en: work is already beginning on another new highway in Boston.
sentences.zh: 波士顿另一条新高速公路的建设已经开始。
它被称为西南高速公路。

sentences.en: And it's important because when linked together,
sentences.zh: 这一点很重要，因为当连结在一起时，

sentences.en: the Southwest Expressway and the inner belt would carry traffic from Interstate 95 straight through the city.
sentences.zh: 西南高速公路和内环路将把来自95号州际公路的车流直接引入城市。

sentences.en: I-95 is the busiest interstate in the whole national system.
sentences.zh: I-95是整个国家系统中最为繁忙的州际公路。

sentences.en: And by 1968, when Nixon is elected president,
sentences.zh: 到1968年尼克松当选总统时，

sentences.en: the road already runs through almost every major city on the East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 这条公路已经穿过了东海岸几乎所有主要城市。

sentences.en: It has cut through Miami's historic black neighborhood of Overtown.
sentences.zh: 它已经穿过了迈阿密历史悠久的黑人社区奥弗敦。

sentences.en: It has cut through New York along the Cross Bronx Expressway.
sentences.zh: 它沿着十字布朗克斯高速公路穿过了纽约。

sentences.en: It has gone through New Haven, Connecticut, Providence, Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 它穿过了康涅狄格州纽黑文、罗德岛州普罗维登斯。

sentences.en: And now its two strands of concrete have literally arrived at the edges of Boston
sentences.zh: 现在它的两条混凝土带径直延伸到了波士顿的边缘，

sentences.en: where they are waiting for the gates to open.
sentences.zh: 在那里等待着闸门开启。

sentences.en: The person holding the keys, so to speak,
sentences.zh: 可以这么说，掌握着钥匙的那个人，

sentences.en: was the brand new governor of Massachusetts, Francis Sargent.
sentences.zh: 正是马萨诸塞州的新任州长弗朗西斯·萨金特。

sentences.en: To change his mind, it would take more than just activists in Cambridge,
sentences.zh: 要改变他的心意，需要的不仅仅是剑桥的活动人士，
再加上一些叛逆的城市规划师。

sentences.en: It would take a coalition, including all the neighborhoods along the Southwest Expressway.
sentences.zh: 它需要一个联盟，包括沿西南高速公路的所有社区。

sentences.en: So we had this very sophisticated strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们制定了这个非常复杂的策略。

sentences.en: We went on to the gas station, got a road map.
sentences.zh: 我们去了加油站，拿了一张公路地图。

sentences.en: And with crayon, we marked out the route of the proposed interstates.
sentences.zh: 用蜡笔勾勒出了拟建州际公路的路线。

sentences.en: And we just went neighborhood by neighborhood, wherever the crayon mark went.
sentences.zh: 我们挨个社区走访，蜡笔画到哪里，我们就走到哪里。

sentences.en: I went to a meeting where a group called Urban Planning Aid
sentences.zh: 我参加了一个会议，一个名为“城市规划援助”的组织
向我们展示了这些被上帝遗弃的规划。

sentences.en: Anne Hirschfang was one of many, many people who heard a version of that presentation.
sentences.zh: 安妮·赫施方是听到过这种演示的众多人之一。

sentences.en: It included drawings of the highways and maps with dark lines superimposed on them.
sentences.zh: 其中包含了高速公路的设计图以及叠加着黑线的地图。

sentences.en: Images that could activate the imagination,
sentences.zh: 这些画面能够激发想象力，

sentences.en: make you realize that the house you had just repainted,
sentences.zh: 让你意识到你刚刚重新粉刷过的房子，

sentences.en: or the block where you knew everyone's kids,
sentences.zh: 或是那个你认识每家每户孩子的街区，

sentences.en: that those things could be taken away and paved over,
sentences.zh: 这些东西都可能会被夺走并铺上柏油，

sentences.en: and no one even needed to so much as ask your opinion.
sentences.zh: 而甚至根本不需要征求一下你的意见。

sentences.en: the person sitting next to Anne volunteered to help spread the word.
sentences.zh: 坐在安妮旁边的那个人自告奋勇要帮忙传播消息。

sentences.en: Then I put up my hand.
I thought, I'm going to do it too.
The Southwest Expressway would cut across three neighborhoods,
sentences.zh: 西南高速公路将穿过三个社区，
每个社区都有其独特的性格。

sentences.en: First, it would enter Boston through a largely white,
sentences.zh: 首先，它将穿过一个主要由白人组成的、
被称为牙买加平原的工人阶级社区进入波士顿。

sentences.en: The state started clearing land there in 1966.
sentences.zh: 州政府于1966年开始在那里清理土地。

sentences.en: I actually went from house to house and took pictures of the abandoned houses.
sentences.zh: 我实际上挨家挨户地去拍了那些被废弃房屋的照片。

sentences.en: Were there still gardens growing in the backyards, flowers?
sentences.zh: 后院里还有菜园和鲜花在生长吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it looked like a normal neighborhood, except there weren't people.
sentences.zh: 是的，它看起来像个正常的社区，只是没有人在里面。

sentences.en: The next neighborhood in the highway's path was Roxbury,
sentences.zh: 高速公路路径上的下一个社区是罗克斯伯里，

sentences.en: the historic center of black culture in Boston.
sentences.zh: 这是波士顿黑人文化历史悠久的中心。

sentences.en: Everybody knows that there are going to be 1,500 jobs that will be taken.
sentences.zh: 人人都知道将有1,500个工作岗位被夺走。

sentences.en: Everybody knows that there will be another 400 homes that will be taken.
sentences.zh: 人人都知道还将有400户住宅被夺走。

sentences.en: We know that there's going to be...
Like in so many cities, Boston's black residents were facing
sentences.zh: 就像在许多城市一样，波士顿的黑人居民正面临着

sentences.en: perhaps the greatest impact from highways.
sentences.zh: 来自高速公路的或许是最具毁灭性的冲击。

sentences.en: Because Roxbury is where the Southwest Expressway
sentences.zh: 因为罗克斯伯里正是西南高速公路

sentences.en: and the inner belt, the spoke and the hub,
sentences.zh: 与内环路，即辐条与枢纽的交汇处，

sentences.en: they were going to meet in a towering five-story interchange.
sentences.zh: 它们将在一个巍峨的五层立交桥处相会。

sentences.en: The fact that 150 acres of developed land
sentences.zh: 事实上，罗克斯伯里-牙买加平原地区

sentences.en: is going to be taken by this four-lane highway.
sentences.zh: 将被这条四车道高速公路占用。

sentences.en: On the other side of that interchange was a third neighborhood, the South End.
sentences.zh: 立交桥的另一侧是第三个社区，南区。

sentences.en: Here, the city started to get more dense
sentences.zh: 在这里，城市开始变得更加稠密，

sentences.en: with rows of old brownstones that were pretty run down in those days.
sentences.zh: 成排的老旧赤褐色砂石建筑在当时已经相当破旧。

sentences.en: It was a neighborhood, approximately one mile square,
sentences.zh: 这是一个面积约一平方英里的社区，

sentences.en: that would have been entirely surrounded by highways.
sentences.zh: 本应完全被高速公路所包围。
你们刚才听到那些声音的主人，

sentences.en: Tom Corrigan, Chuck Turner, and Ken Krukmeyer,
sentences.zh: 汤姆·科里根、查克·特纳和肯·克鲁克迈尔，

sentences.en: were to all end up involved with a new umbrella organization,
sentences.zh: 最终都参与了一个新的总括性组织，

sentences.en: the Greater Boston Committee on the Transportation Crisis,
sentences.zh: 大波士顿交通危机委员会，

sentences.en: But as the coalition grew, it also became more unwieldy.
sentences.zh: 但随着联盟的壮大，它也变得越来越难以管理。

sentences.en: Each neighborhood had its own particular issues with the highways
sentences.zh: 每个社区对高速公路都有自己具体的问题

sentences.en: There's a story of Chuck Turner showing up for a protest
sentences.zh: 有个故事说，查克·特纳现身参加一个抗议活动，
地点在一个主要由意大利人组成的社区，

sentences.en: dressed in a dashiki and carrying a poster of Malcolm X.
sentences.zh: 身穿达什基长衫，手拿马尔科姆·X的海报。

sentences.en: Some residents were grateful for the solidarity.
sentences.zh: 一些居民对这种声援表示感激。

sentences.en: To help unify all the various factions,
sentences.zh: 为了帮助团结各方派别，

sentences.en: the GBC took a very simple position.
sentences.zh: 大波士顿委员会采取了非常明确的立场。

sentences.en: No new highways in Greater Boston, period.
sentences.zh: 大波士顿地区绝不修建新高速公路，就这样。

sentences.en: The days of debating routes were officially over.
sentences.zh: 争论路线的日子已经正式结束了。

sentences.en: And the strategy of this new group was right in the name.
sentences.zh: 而这个新组织的策略就直接体现在它的名字里。

sentences.en: Make this an issue for all of Greater Boston,
sentences.zh: 将这变成整个大波士顿地区的问题，
而不仅仅是三个街区的事。

sentences.en: That's how you get the governor's attention.
sentences.zh: 这就是引起州长注意的方法。

sentences.en: I had the set of slides in a carousel,
sentences.zh: 我把幻灯片装在一个圆盘盒里，

sentences.en: and a whole group of us spread out over the entire metropolitan area
sentences.zh: 我们的一大群人分散到整个大都市区，

sentences.en: and tell people about the plans for the highway.
sentences.zh: 向人们讲述高速公路的规划。

sentences.en: And everywhere they went, they found people who wanted to listen.
sentences.zh: 他们所到之处，都能找到愿意倾听的人。

sentences.en: Here's Chuck Turner, one of the lead activists in Roxbury,
sentences.zh: 这位是查克·特纳，罗克斯伯里主要的活动人士之一，
正在一次公开会议上发言。

sentences.en: You know, in this country, it's a strange thing that if you look on issues,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这个国家，奇怪的是，如果你看看各种议题，

sentences.en: you usually see black people fighting white people.
sentences.zh: 你通常会看到黑人在与白人抗争。

sentences.en: You usually see the rich against the poor.
sentences.zh: 你通常会看到富人反对穷人。

sentences.en: You usually see the suburbanites against people in the inner city.
sentences.zh: 你通常会看到郊区居民反对市中心居民。

sentences.en: It's strange when you see one issue and all those people are united and saying,
sentences.zh: 当你看到一个问题，而所有这些人都团结起来说

sentences.en: we don't want to build and we're going to stop it.
sentences.zh: 我们不想修建，我们要阻止它，这就很奇怪。

sentences.en: And Governor Sargent and no other political official in this state
sentences.zh: 萨金特州长以及本州的任何其他政治官员

sentences.en: is going to be able to build the highway over that objection.
sentences.zh: 都不可能在面临这种反对的情况下修建这条高速公路。

sentences.en: By January of 1969, when Francis Sargent took his oath as governor,
sentences.zh: 到1969年1月弗朗西斯·萨金特宣誓就职州长时，
大波士顿委员会的抗议者们已经准备就绪。

sentences.en: About 2,000 folks show up in front of the statehouse saying,
sentences.zh: 大约两千人出现在州议会大厦前，高喊着

sentences.en: what are you going to do about this road?
sentences.zh: 你们打算如何处理这条路？

sentences.en: What are you going to do about this, Sargent?
sentences.zh: 萨金特，你打算怎么处理这事？

sentences.en: What had started as a small group of Cambridge residents pushing back
sentences.zh: 最初由一小群剑桥居民发起、

sentences.en: against a single road had grown into a radical challenge
sentences.zh: 反对单条道路的反抗，已经演变成了一场对

sentences.en: to the state's entire road building policy.
sentences.zh: 全州道路建设计划的激进挑战。

sentences.en: And this was the coming out party for the movement.
sentences.zh: 这是这场运动的首次正式亮相。

sentences.en: All the players, all the factions gathered in one place.
sentences.zh: 所有参与者、所有派别都聚集在一个地方。

sentences.en: It spilled down the stairs of the statehouse over into Boston Common.
sentences.zh: 人群从州议会大厦的台阶一直蔓延到波士顿公园。

sentences.en: People from every neighborhood in Boston.
sentences.zh: 波士顿各个街区的人都来了。

sentences.en: Anstie Benfield led a march over from Cambridge and addressed the crowd.
